messages:
alice: heads up — onboarding a community Llama variant hit a weird downstream with our multi-model routing. model runs fine standalone but when routed through adapter chain we see token misalignments and strange logits.
ben: hmm — misalignments in what sense? are tokens shifted or embedding mismatch?
alice: tokens shift. reproducer: run pipeline with model A (llama->quant int4) then swap to model B (mistral-compiled) mid-session. kv-cache offsets look ok, but rotary-based attention gives garbled completions.
charlie: do you have a diff of kv keys or head ordering? could be head permutation/stride mismatch.
alice: I dumped first few kvcache keys. snippet:
```
# after switch
kvs[0][:8] = [0x1f2a, 0x1f2b, 0x1f2c, ...]
# expected
kvs_expected[0][:8] = [0x1f2a, 0x1f2b, 0x1f2c, ...]
# but rotary phase matrix differs per head
rotary_phases_modelA = [0.0, 0.5, 1.0, ...]
rotary_phases_modelB = [0.0, 0.5, 0.999, ...]
```
ben: tiny numeric diff in phase shouldn't blow things up unless head-to-head mapping is wrong.
diane: quick check — are we using per-head scaling vs per-tensor scaling in the compiled kernels? mismatch there can look like phase drift.
charlie: also check tokenizer normalization. I recently saw NFKC vs NFC causing different token ids for soft hyphen on Qwen -> downstream cache aliasing.
alice: good point. I ran `python -m tokencheck` across models: Qwen normalizes to NFKC, gemma/llama kept identity. small diacritics re-tokenized into different ids.
ben: so two orthogonal problems: tokenizer normalization -> token id aliasing, and rotary/head order -> permutation. both can cause bad cache reuse.
diane: any quantization-related signal? int4 kernels might reorder columns for packing; if we reuse kvcache shapes between quantized and fp16 variants we'll see index mismatch.
alice: yes, in our quant experiments we observed that int4 export uses grouped-head packing; the adapter assumed contiguous head dims.
charlie: can we workaround at routing layer: invalidate kv-cache on model variant switch (cheap) and re-tokenize with canonical normalizer? might be OK for now.
infra-bot: deploy note: rolled route change to invalidate kvcache-on-switch on canary (eng-ml-canary) at 16:45 UTC :rocket:
alice: thanks infra-bot. more followups: eval runs show perplexity jump ~3x and nll spikes on few-shot summarization after switch.
eval-bot: eval summary: 50-shot summarization test: baseline (no switch) avg-BLEU 28.1, after-invalidate avg-BLEU 27.9, without-invalidate 9.3. regression concentrated in long context prompts (>1024 tokens).
ben: big delta. So invalidation fixes most of it — points to cache aliasing vs model quality.
diane: longer term we should canonicalize tokenizer pipeline in model spec (normalization form + sentinel handling) and annotate export metadata: head-order, rotary-params, packed-head-layout.
charlie: agreed. we can add a quick spec fields: token_norm: NFKC|NFC|NONE, head_layout: contiguous|packed, rotary_format: per_head|per_pair, kvstride: value. then routing checks compatibility before allowing cache reuse.
alice: I'll draft a PR with patches: (1) invalidate-on-variant-switch by default, (2) model metadata checks in routing, (3) a small token-normalizer shim for legacy models.
ben: also add a unit test: start session on model X, append tokens that re-tokenize differently under Y, then attempt switch and assert cache invalidation. add a perf guard for extra invalidations.
diane: can someone run a quick sweep of our onboarded models and flag ones with nonstandard token_norm or packed-head-layout? I can own coordination.
alice: I'll run a scanner today and post results here. initial targets: gemma-lite, qwen-variants, mistralx builds.
charlie: thanks team. small note — when we re-enable cache reuse, we should fuzz check kv keys and rotary phases within epsilon, otherwise silently subtle errors.
alice: agreed. will include epsilon checks and logging to make future triage faster. cc @diane for rollout plan.
